In addition, noise measurements were taken for a 24 hour period on the roof of Hamlin Garland School. The hourly noise variations are shown in Figure 21. The noise levels ranged from 55 to 64 dBA. The noise levels during late evening and early morning hours were considerably lower than noise levels during the day time.
During this 24 hour period, simultaneous indoor and outdoor noise measurements were taken in order to determine the attenuation characteristics of Hamlin Garland School. The classroom selected in the northwest corner of the school building is located closest to both I-94 and the proposed Airport Spur, and should represent the highest indoor noise levels due to freeway traffic. This classroom represents the typical layout and construction of those in the school.
The 
L_{10}
 noise level recorded outside the school building was 64dBA while the inside ranged from 41dBA with the windows closed and 50 dBA with the windows open. Therefore, the school can typically provide 23 dBA attenuation with the windows closed and 14 dBA attenuation with the windows open.
In a noise study conducted in 1970 by the Milwaukee Public Schools, noise measurements at Hamlin Garland School ranged from 69-90dBC. These noise measurements however, were not taken on the nationally accepted A-weighted scale nor with the precision necessary to consider them conclusive. Therefore a subsequent study was conducted in 1974 by the Milwaukee Public Schools. The 
L_{10}
 noise measurement was 64 dBA.
